questions.q_en: If M is a positive integer and M > 2, then what will be the greatest number which is exactly divides every number of the form (M3 - M)(M - 2)?
questions.solution_en:
M is a positive integer and M > 2.

Putting, M = 3, => (33 - 3)(3 - 2) = 24

Putting, M = 4, => (43 - 4)(4 - 2) = 120

Putting, M = 5, => (53 - 5)(5 - 2) = 360

Hence, it is always divisible by 24.

Upstream speed of boat = 80/10 = 8 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = (10 + 8)/2

= 9 km/h

questions.q_en: In a 300 meters race, X defeats Y by 20 meters and Y defeats Z by 15 meters. By what distance will X defeats Z in the same race?
questions.solution_en:
When X covers 300 => Y covers 300 - 20 = 280

When Y covers 300 => Z covers 300 - 15 = 285

X/Y = 300/280 = 15/14 and Y/Z = 300/285 = 20/19

X/Z = (15/14) * (20/19) = 300/266

X defeats Z in the same race by => 300 - 266 = 34 meters

Since, ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR which means all the corresponding sides and angles will be equal.

And,

questions.q_en: A man sells a mobile phone for ₹680 and loses something. If he had sold it for ₹1070, his gain would have been double the former loss. The cost price (in ₹) of the mobile phone is:
questions.solution_en:
Let the loss be ₹X.

Selling price = ₹680

Cost price = 680 + X

New selling price = ₹1070

Profit = 2X

Cost price = 1070 - 2X

Now,

680 + X = 1070 - 2X

3X = 390

X = 130

Cost price of the mobile phone = 680 + 130 = ₹810

Hence option c is not divisible by 11.

Option d:

Hence option d is not divisible by 11.

What should the new selling price be to maintain the same 30% profit?
questions.solution_en:
Gain% = (SP - CP)/CP * 100

Let the cost price of 1000 gram of rice is Rs. p

Cost price of 800 gram of rice = x/1000 * 800 = Rs. 4x/5

To earn a profit of 30% the selling price should be :

=> 4x/5 * 130/100 = 1.04x

questions.q_en: Ramesh and Suresh starts in the same direction from the same point around a circular track. They both start at the same time and Ramesh who runs faster than Suresh catches him 425 meters away from the starting point. If the ratio of their speeds is 2 : 7 then what is the total length of the track?
questions.solution_en:
Let the diameter of the track be d' meter hence total length of the track will be '2d' meters.

When first time Ramesh catches Suresh then total distance travelled by Suresh = 425 m

Since both are running from the same point in the same direction hence Ramesh will catch Suresh for the 1st time when he has travelled one complete round more than Suresh.

Hence total distance travelled by Ramesh when they met for the 1st time = (2d + 425) m

According to the question we will get; 425/(2d+425)=2/7

=> 7 X 425 = 2(2d + 425)

=>2975 = 4d + 850

=> 2d = 1062.5

Hence total length of the track is 1062.5 m.

questions.q_en: A train crosses a person standing at a point in 20 sec. If the person was running alongside with the train at 21.6 km/hr, then the train would have crossed him in 25 sec. What is the length of the train (in metres)?
questions.solution_en:
Let speed and length of the train be 'v' m/s and 'd' m respectively.

d = 20v

If the person was running, relative speed = v - 21.6 * (5/18) = v - 6

d = 25(v - 6)

20v = 25v - 150

5v = 150

v = 30

So, d = 20 * 30 = 600 metres

questions.q_en: If the sum of two numbers is 32 and the product of those numbers is 255, then the sum of their squares is equal to:
Find the least number which when divided by 12, 15, 18, and 30 leaves a remainder 3 in each case, but is exactly divisible by 11.
questions.solution_en:
Factor of 12 = 22 * 3

Factor of 15 = 3 * 5

Factor of 18 = 2 * 32

Factor of 30 = 2 * 3 * 5

LCM = 22 * 32 * 5 = 180

Number will be 180k + 3 (k is an integer)

Try k = 1

=> 180 * 1 + 3 = 183 (Not divisible by 11)

Try k = 2

=> 180 * 2 + 3 = 363 (divisible by 11)

Least number = 363

questions.q_en: A merchant bought two watches for ₹9,000 each. He sold one watch at a loss of 10%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the other watch to earn a profit of 18% overall?
questions.solution_en:
Total cost price = 2*9000 = ₹18000

Overall selling price = 118% of 18000 = ₹21240

Selling price of one watch = 90% of 9000 = ₹8100

Selling price of other watch = 21240 - 8100 = ₹13140
